subject: Audit follow-up: management response, evidence timeline, and bridge letter request
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@echohealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: soc.audit@brightassurance.com
Date: 2026-06-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOC2: follow-up on control exception and expected evidence timeline

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our audit team flagged one open item related to control 202 (change management documentation for the June patch window) in your SOC 2 Type II submissions. Bright Assurance asked us to capture Redwood's management response and an estimated remediation timeline so they can close the exception for EchoHealth's report.

Can you confirm the current status, who owns the remediation, and whether you can provide interim evidence (logs or approvals) for the audit period? Also, our compliance team asked if Redwood could provide a bridge letter confirming there were no additional compensating control failures outside the documented exception between 2026-05-01 and 2026-06-30. That would help us avoid an adverse finding in our external report.

Appreciate a short note and any artifacts you can share by next Wednesday (2026-07-07).

Best,
Lydia Park
Head of Procurement, EchoHealth

--
EchoHealth | procurement@echohealth.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@echohealth.com>, soc.audit@brightassurance.com
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2: follow-up on control exception and expected evidence timeline

Hi Lydia (and Bright Assurance team),

Thanks for the heads up. Short summary up front: we own the remediation (Rishi is the tech lead), the change that triggered the exception was a rollout on 2026-06-12 that skipped a required documented approval step due to a monitoring alert routing change. We have a remediation plan in place and can provide interim evidence.

Planned next steps:
- Today (07/01): Rishi will snapshot the deploy approvals and compile the rollback/mitigation notes.
- By 07/07: we will upload initial artifacts (approval screenshots, deploy runbook excerpt, and related logs) to a shared evidence folder.
- By 07/20: complete remediation (formalize the approval gate in CI and add an automated alert for missing approvals) and provide final evidence and a management response letter.

We can provide a draft bridge letter for your review this week. I am attaching a draft and a zipped packet of the current artifacts we have collected. If Bright Assurance needs anything signed/dated differently, let us know and we will adapt.

Attachments: 20260701-vk-snapshot-approvals.pdf, 20260701-control202-evidence.zip

Please see the short notes below from Rishi on technical ownership.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Sent: 2026-07-01T10:01:00-07:00
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Subject: control-202 quick notes

We routed on-call alerts differently during a config push; approval flow integrations were temporarily bypassed for emergency monitoring. Ownership: infra-deploy team (Marissa), remediation owner to add the CI gate back and produce an automated verification job. Estimate: gating and automated verification completed by 07/20, low-risk. Logs included in the zip show the approval insertion point and timestamped actions.

-Rishi
From: soc.audit@brightassurance.com <soc.audit@brightassurance.com>
To: Vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, lydia.park@echohealth.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-07T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2: follow-up on control exception and expected evidence timeline

Hi all,

We received the initial artifacts in the Drive link you sent. A couple of quick clarifications before we can accept the interim evidence:
- The approval screenshots are time-stamped but do not show the approver identity string in one of the captures; we need either a full audit log entry or a signed statement confirming the approver identity.
- For the bridge letter, we need explicit language that the exception described pertains only to the documented deploy on 2026-06-12 and that no other control deviations were identified during the period 2026-05-01 to 2026-06-30. The letter should be on company letterhead and include the signer's title and date.

If you can update the evidence folder with a redacted audit log extract and provide a dated bridge letter draft, we can proceed with closing the exception in our final report conditional on remediation completion by 07/20.

Thanks,
Bright Assurance SOC Team
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: soc.audit@brightassurance.com, lydia.park@echohealth.com
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2: follow-up on control exception and expected evidence timeline

Hi Lydia and Bright Assurance,

Attached is the requested bridge letter draft on Redwood letterhead (filename: 20260715-vk-bridge-letter-draft.pdf). It states explicitly that the documented exception relates solely to the 2026-06-12 deploy and that we identified no other control deviations within the audit period of 2026-05-01 to 2026-06-30. The letter includes the signer's name (Avery Johnson, VP Security), title, and date placeholder.

I've also uploaded a redacted audit log extract that includes approver identity strings and timestamps to the shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-echohealth-evidence. The evidence zip now contains: control202-approver-log-redacted.csv, deploy-runbook-excerpt.pdf, remediation-plan.md.

Next actions:
- 07/20: final remediation proofs uploaded and formal sign-off letter countersigned by Avery.
- If Bright Assurance wants a notarized bridge letter, we can accommodate but will need a couple of extra business days.

Let us know if the bridge letter draft meets formatting expectations; we can move to a signed PDF once you confirm language.

Regards,
Vivek

Attachments: 20260715-vk-bridge-letter-draft.pdf, 20260715-control-202-evidence-updated.zip
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@echohealth.com>
To: Vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, soc.audit@brightassurance.com
Date: 2026-07-20T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2: follow-up on control exception and expected evidence timeline

Vivek — this is perfect, thanks for the quick turnaround. Bright Assurance confirmed the redacted log and the bridge letter language are sufficient for conditional closure. They will accept the exception as closed once the remediation evidence is uploaded on 07/20 and the final sign-off letter is countersigned.

I'll mark this as resolved on EchoHealth's side pending the final uploads. Please send the signed bridge letter PDF and final remediation artifacts when available.

Best,
Lydia

--
Lydia Park | EchoHealth
